summary: This note gives a historical overview of the major over-the-air television networks in the United States. For most of broadcasting history there were only three or four major commercial national networks. From 1946 to 1956 these were ABC, CBS, NBC and DuMont, with Paramount Television Network having limited success, and from 1956 to 1986 the Big Three were ABC, CBS and NBC. It also notes National Educational Television as the public TV clearinghouse from 1954 to 1970, succeeded by PBS.
one_line: Overview of the history of major US over-the-air television networks, from the DuMont era through the Big Three to public broadcasting.
key_facts: For most of the history of broadcasting in the United States, there were only three or four major commercial national broadcast networks.
From 1946 to 1956, the major commercial national networks were ABC, CBS, NBC and DuMont.
The Paramount Television Network had some limited success during 1946 to 1956.
From 1956 to 1986, the 'Big Three' national commercial networks were ABC, CBS, and NBC.
National Telefilm Associates and its NTA Film Network were a limited attempt to challenge the Big Three.
The Overmyer Network was a limited attempt to challenge the Big Three.
From 1954 to 1970, National Educational Television was the national clearinghouse for public TV programming.
The Public Broadcasting Service (PBS) succeeded National Educational Television in 1970.
